shortlist.story: A new clinical trial is testing an AI phone assistant that checks in on patients living with long-term illnesses.
shortlist.best_title: New trial of AI phone assistant to monitor patients with long-term illness
shortlist.why: The word 'trial' signals something has started; AI is clearly the monitoring tool; real patients with chronic conditions are the subject, not the AI industry itself.

shortlist.story: A randomised clinical trial called PARAMOUNT found that AI-guided plaque-based heart care met its primary endpoint, presented at AHA 2026.
shortlist.best_title: PARAMOUNT, the First Randomized Trial of AI-Enabled Plaque-Based Care, Meets Primary Endpoint in Late-Breaking Results at AHA 2026
shortlist.why: A named RCT with a reported primary endpoint is strong evidence; presented at a major cardiology conference; AI is the specific intervention, not incidental; about patient health outcomes.

shortlist.story: WeCare's AI chatbot is currently enabling three GPs to manage a patient load of 30,000 people.
shortlist.best_title: WeCare's chatbot lets three GPs carry 30,000 patients
shortlist.why: Present tense 'lets' implies current deployment; specific numbers suggest real evidence; AI is the direct reason a small team can cover the load; clearly about healthcare delivery, not AI industry.

shortlist.story: UAE researchers have built and deployed an AI system to track marine biodiversity in the Arabian Gulf.
shortlist.best_title: UAE Researchers Develop AI System to Monitor Marine Biodiversity in the Arabian Gulf
shortlist.why: Past tense 'develop' indicates completion; AI is the instrument; about environmental monitoring in a named real-world body of water, not AI industry news.

shortlist.story: A new AI study found that severe wildfires can increase snowpack downstream, but also identified why that effect does not offset broader climate harm.
shortlist.best_title: Severe wildfire left more snow on the ground, but a new AI study shows why that is not the whole story
shortlist.why: Study is completed; AI drove the analysis that produced a nuanced climate finding; subject is the natural world, not the AI sector.

shortlist.story: Agentic AI is now being used to scan radio signals as part of the search for extraterrestrial intelligence.
shortlist.best_title: Agentic AI Joins the Search for Extraterrestrial Signals
shortlist.why: Present-tense 'joins' implies something has started; AI is the specific new capability enabling signal analysis at scale; space/science topic well outside AI industry.

shortlist.story: Howard University and Google Research published research aimed at reducing the bias in AI speech recognition systems that disadvantages Black American speakers.
shortlist.best_title: Howard University and Google Research Address AI Speech Bias Against Black Americans
shortlist.why: Research published, so something happened; AI is both the source of the problem and the site of the fix; directly concerns a named, real population; accessibility/fairness outcome.

shortlist.story: Lighthouse Guild is deploying Meta's AI-powered smart glasses with blind veterans to help them overcome everyday barriers.
shortlist.best_title: Lighthouse Guild partners with Meta to help blind veterans overcome barriers using AI glasses
shortlist.why: Partnership implies current use; real people (blind veterans) are named; AI glasses are the specific tool making the difference; accessibility outcome, not an industry announcement.

shortlist.story: A fire department tried AI to address a longstanding recruitment problem and the headline implies it worked.
shortlist.best_title: Did Artificial Intelligence Solve the Fire Department Recruitment Conundrum?
shortlist.why: Rhetorical 'did…?' with 'solve' implies a positive result was reported; real institution, public-safety outcome; AI is the stated reason; worth opening to confirm.

shortlist.story: Texas A&M researchers used AI to identify new disease targets hidden among hundreds of previously mysterious proteins inside mitochondria.
shortlist.best_title: Artificial intelligence points researchers toward new disease targets hidden in mitochondria
shortlist.why: Clear lab result from a named institution via EurekaAlert; AI is the specific tool that made the discovery possible; medical science finding with real-world implications.

shortlist.story: Researchers used a physics-informed AI framework to convert ordinary fibre-optic communication cables into large-scale highway traffic sensors, requiring no new infrastructure.
shortlist.best_title: Turning fiber-optic cables into traffic sensors: A new physics-informed AI approach for highway monitoring
shortlist.why: Research result published; AI is what makes the repurposing work; everyday-life application; surprising reuse of existing cables; plainly explainable.

shortlist.story: Weill Cornell disclosed that radiology patients' medical records were fed into AI tools without authorisation — the institution itself made the disclosure.
shortlist.best_title: Weill Cornell Says Radiology Patients' Medical Details Were Entered Into AI Tools Without Authorization
shortlist.why: Owning-up flip: a named institution publicly disclosed its own AI data-handling failure; no patient was physically harmed; the good side — institutional transparency — is a separate documented fact, not spin.

shortlist.story: Employers who mandated AI tool use are now publicly admitting the approach backfired, suggesting a course-correction is under way.
shortlist.best_title: Remember When Bosses Were Forcing Their Workers to Use AI? They're Now Realizing They Made a Huge Mistake
shortlist.why: Owning-up flip: employers acknowledging a mistake is itself a good-side fact; widely covered bad story (forced AI mandates); no physical injury; good side is documented employer recalibration, not mere opinion.
